_comment: darkmux profile registry — example. Three worker profiles in increasing capacity order (fast → balanced → deep), plus one example of a model on an endpoint darkmux only sends requests to. A profile's `models[]` are WORKER models; the machine's one utility model (compaction, radio routing) lives once in the top-level `internal.utility` with its own `n_ctx`, and is never selectable for a task. `n_ctx` is required for models darkmux loads (it is the load parameter) and omitted for models on an endpoint darkmux does not manage. Endpoints are declared once under `endpoints` (url, `managed`, `dialect`, `auth` naming where the credential lives, and `limits`: a rolling `window` budget (e.g. `"period": "1d", "tokens": 2000000`, the last 24 hours from now) whose `policy` says what reaching it does: `warn` (the default once a budget is set) or `wait` (pause calls to that endpoint until the window has room), or `off`. darkmux ships no budget: every number is unset here, and nothing is counted until you set one) and named by id from a model; a model with no `endpoint` is sent to the LM Studio at `lmstudio_url`, which darkmux manages. `darkmux init` fills the `<your-worker-model-id>` slots from a model you have downloaded; run `lms ls` to see them, and `darkmux config set role_profiles.<role> <profile>` to staff a mission seat. Profiles for the review mission's `reviewer` seat are in the guide, not here.

fast.description: Single-turn tasks. Slim worker — fastest dispatch, lowest RAM.

balanced.description: Mid-range tasks. Predictable behavior across mixed workloads; compaction runs on the machine's internal.utility model.

deep.description: Long agentic tasks. Maximum worker context for fewer compactions.

hosted-frontier.description: A model on an endpoint darkmux only sends requests to (declared under `endpoints` below and named by id) — no n_ctx: whatever serves the endpoint owns the context window. Delete this profile, and the `azure-openai` endpoint, if you only run models darkmux manages.
